Kim / Marissa — quick technical addendum to include with the package (sending as internal follow-up):

- Cryptographic key custody: pseudonymization is performed using a per-customer AEAD envelope key. Key wrapping performed in KMS; keys are non-exportable. (See sheet: KeyCustody in pseudonymization-matrix.xlsx)
- Reversibility: mapping table indicates whether reversible tokenization is in use. Default production flow uses non-reversible hashing for high-risk PII; reversible tokens are available only for opt-in customers under contract and require KMS unwrap.
- Model handling: training datasets are isolated; no customer-supplied PII is used for model weights unless customer enables controlled fine-tune via explicit consent and data mapping. We will include operational runbook excerpt (redacted).
- Art. 30 excerpt: we will provide a CSV extract with processing categories and subprocessor list; note that subprocessor inventory includes cloud providers and monitoring vendors — a separate subprocessor evidence packet is available on request.

I uploaded a short checklist and links to the secured drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cRD-pseudonymization-evidence (access can be restricted to view-only). If the auditor needs remote access, we can provide time-limited credentials and a read-only environment for log review.

Ben Carter
Security Engineer, Privacy Controls
Redwood Inference
